headline: Memory And Chips Become AI's New Center Of Gravity
paragraph: Capital has rotated from the agent narrative toward the physical layer underneath it. SK Hynix's $26.5B IPO — the largest foreign listing in Wall Street history — and a $550B Korean chip commitment mark a hardware supercycle even as model releases keep accelerating (GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, Muse Spark). Meanwhile the leading labs show internal strain: OpenAI lost its No. 2 and safety chief in one week while Apple sued it over trade secrets. Security incidents and regulatory pressure are both climbing, signaling that governance is not keeping pace with deployment.
bullets: SK Hynix's $26.5B IPO plus a $550B Korean chip-supply commitment confirm the capital center has moved to memory and compute — agents' monthly topic share fell to 9.5% from a 32.7% February peak.

Model velocity is up sharply (benchmarks_evals momentum +176%) with GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, and Muse Spark shipping in the same week — price/performance competition is compressing frontier-lab margins faster than expected.

OpenAI's No. 2 Fidji Simo stepped back and its safety head departed within days of Apple filing a trade-secret suit — leadership and legal instability at the industry's bellwether just as it scales ChatGPT Work.
Security incidents hold near 15.5% share of coverage: an AI-run ransomware attack and a GitHub Copilot data-leak exploit show agentic systems are outrunning their own guardrails.

Big Tech is cutting cost even as chip capex explodes — Microsoft cut 4,800 jobs and is insourcing its own models, Amazon shut new sign-ups for Mechanical Turk — a squeeze on labor and third-party spend beneath the hardware boom.
